# Weather Aggregator — Agent Protocol

This site aggregates multiple public, no-API-key weather forecast models for one
kind of decision: whether outdoor conditions at a chosen place and date range are
favorable. It does not make the decision. It assembles the inputs.

This file is an index and protocol doc. The data lives in the JSON endpoints below.
URLs here are relative to the origin this file was served from.

## Fetch the data (preferred)

Served by the site's Cloudflare Worker, which queries the models server-side.
Same-origin, no key, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, pretty-printed JSON. They
work even if your environment blocks external weather APIs (e.g. api.open-meteo.com)
or cannot run JavaScript.

Start here — the index lists ABSOLUTE links to every per-day file, so a single
fetch gives you URLs your fetch tool will accept:

  /forecast/index.json

Other endpoints:

  /forecast.json                       all days: every daytime hour's consensus +
                                       spread, no per-model arrays
  /forecast/YYYY-MM-DD.summary.json    one day: per-hour consensus + model spread
  /forecast/YYYY-MM-DD.json            one day: every model's hourly values, for
                                       model-by-model attribution

## Choosing the place and dates

Query params, accepted by every endpoint:

- `city` — "City", "City, State" or "City, Country", e.g. `?city=Burlington, VT`
  or `?city=Lyon, France`. US state and Canadian province abbreviations work.
  The best match is used and echoed back in `location.name`; check it.
- `lat` + `lon` — decimal degrees, used when `city` is absent.
- `start` + `end` — `YYYY-MM-DD`, both required if either is given.

Defaults: Québec City, Canada (lat 46.8139, lon -71.2080), today and tomorrow in
the location's own timezone.

Date limits: the underlying models only cover a rolling window from about 92 days
in the past to 15 days in the future. Outside it you get HTTP 400 with
`error: "invalid_dates"` or `"dates_out_of_range"`. Later dates become available
as they come within 15 days. Other errors: 404 `city_not_found`, 400
`invalid_coordinates`, 502 `forecast_failed` (upstream trouble — retry). A per-day
URL for a date outside the requested range returns `error: "date_not_found"` with
the list of `available` dates.

The per-day links in `perDayFiles` carry the same query params you sent, so they
stay aimed at the same place and dates.

Always pull fresh. There is NO server-side caching — every request rebuilds from
the latest Open-Meteo data and is returned with `Cache-Control: no-store`. If your
own fetch tool caches responses by URL, append a throwaway query param such as
`&t=1719700000`; unknown params are ignored by the server. `generatedAt` (ISO)
stamps each build; `snapshotHash` tells you if anything actually changed.

## If you are running the page in a browser instead

The same full payload is at `window.__WEATHER_FORECAST__` after a forecast loads,
and in the `<script id="forecastData" type="application/json">` tag. "Export JSON"
downloads it. Fetching the raw HTML alone returns empty tables — the UI renders
client-side.

## Context

- Location, timezone and date range are echoed in every payload under `location`
  and `range`. All times are local to the location.
- Units: temperature °F, wind mph, precipitation inch.
- Only daytime hours (08:00–21:00 local) are scored and returned.

## Data sources

Open-Meteo serves several independent models behind one endpoint. We query and
compare these. `best_match` is Open-Meteo's blend and is reported separately —
spread is computed across the 8 independent models only, so the blend never
narrows the honest range.

- best_match (blend — excluded from spread)
- ecmwf_ifs025, gfs_global, gem_global, icon_global  (physics models)
- ecmwf_aifs025, gfs_graphcast025  (ML models)
- ukmo_global_deterministic_10km, meteofrance_arpege_world

Environment Canada's city page collection is queried only as a source-health
sanity check, not scored. It appears in `sourceHealth` only when the location
has a nearby Canadian city page.

## JSON schema (key fields)

Top level: `generatedAt`, `snapshotHash`, `location`, `range`, `units`,
`sourceCount`, `independentCount`, `note`, `verdict`, `days[]`, `hours[]`,
`sourceHealth[]`.

`snapshotHash` is a 64-bit content hash of the decision-relevant outputs (rounded,
so trivial float jitter doesn't flip it). Use it two ways: (1) two files with the
same hash describe the same forecast run, so index and a summary fetched together
should match — if they don't, refetch; (2) compare against the hash from your last
fetch to know whether the forecast materially changed or is just noise. Same hash =
nothing decision-relevant moved, even if generatedAt is newer.

`verdict`: `signal` (one of: mostly favorable | leaning favorable | mixed |
mostly unfavorable — a neutral description of the data, not advice),
`avgTripScore`, `favorableDays`, `comfortableDays`, `poorDays`,
`comfortableHours`, `stormDays[]` (ISO dates), `lowAgreementDays`, `facts[]`.

`days[]` per day: `date`, `avgScore` (0–100), `rating`, `label`, `excellentHours`
(score ≥75), `goodHours` (score ≥60), `excellentStretch`/`goodStretch` (longest
continuous hours), `maxFeels` °F, `maxGust` mph, `avgHumidity` %, `agreement`
(high|medium|low|insufficient sources), `stormPeak` (max models agreeing on a
thunderstorm in any hour), `stormStart`, `periods[]` (morning/afternoon/evening
scores), `bestExcellentWindow`/`bestGoodWindow`, `planLine` (factual summary).

`hours[]` per daytime hour: `time` (local ISO), `date`, `hour`, `score`, `rating`,
`label`, `temp`, `feels`, `humidity`, `windGusts`, `rainSignal` (mean rain prob %),
`rainMin`/`rainMax`/`rainSpread`, `agreement`, `stormVotes`/`showerVotes` (model
counts), `sourceCount`, `independentCount`,
`spread`: `{ rainProb, feels, gust }`, each `{ min, max, median, n }` across
independent models — `n` is how many models actually reported that metric this
hour (some models return nulls for some fields, so n can be < independentCount;
trust a spread less when n is small). `blend`: best_match's
`{ feels, rainProb, windGusts, code }`. `models[]` (full per-day files only):
each model's `{ id, label, independent, feels, rainProb, precip, showers, gust,
humidity, code }`.

`index.json`/`forecast.json` also carry `perDayFiles`: a map of date ->
`{ summary, full }` absolute URLs. `summary`/`full` payloads carry `tier`.

## How the comfort score works (heuristic, not a physical model)

Each hour starts at 100 and subtracts penalties: mean rain probability ×0.48;
measured precipitation (up to −35); showers (up to −25); a saturating thunderstorm
penalty (WMO 95/96/99) of −16 for the first model reporting one and −7 for each
further model, capped at −38; −4 per model reporting shower codes (80/81/82);
apparent temp >88°F and >82°F penalties; humidity >82% penalty; wind gusts >24 mph
(up to −14); −4 when models disagree strongly. Bands: ≥75 favorable, ≥60 generally
comfortable, ≥42 mixed, <42 unfavorable. The score is tuned for warm-season
walking comfort: it does not penalize cold, so read `temp`/`feels` directly in
cold weather.

Day score = 45% of the daytime hourly average + 30% of the average of the better
half of the hours, plus a bonus for long CONTINUOUS comfortable/favorable blocks
(a 4-hour clear stretch beats four scattered clear hours), minus small penalties
for scattered good hours and for model disagreement.

## Model agreement (not "confidence")

`agreement` measures how much the independent models diverge for an hour/day — it
says nothing about whether the forecast is correct, only how converged the models
are. Derived from the standard deviation and range of rain probability plus the
range of apparent temperature. Bands: high ≤25, medium ≤45, else low; with <3
models, "insufficient sources". Low agreement = treat those values as soft,
especially on later (further-out) days.

## Suggested use

1. Fetch `/forecast/index.json` for the shape, then per-day files as needed.
2. Report the spread (min–max), not just the mean — the range is the honest signal.
3. Flag hours where `stormVotes` ≥3.
4. Call out low-`agreement` days as uncertain; note later dates have more lead time.
5. Summarize per day: longest continuous comfortable block, peak feels-like, peak
   gust, storm presence and timing.
6. Present the numbers and let the human decide. Avoid prescriptive verdicts.
